import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 160

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/160](https://www.erdosproblems.com/160)
-/

namespace Erdos160

/--
Let $h(n)$ be the smallest $k$ such that $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ can be coloured with $k$ colours
so that every four-term arithmetic progression must contain at least three distinct colours.
-/
noncomputable def erdos_160.h (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
    sInf {k | ∃ (colouring : Finset.Icc 1 n → Fin k), ∀ (progression : Set ℕ),
    (progression ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n ∧ progression.IsAPOfLength 4) →
    3 ≤ (colouring '' {k | (k : ℕ) ∈ progression}).ncard}


open Filter

/--
On [Mathoverflow](https://mathoverflow.net/a/410815) user
[leechlattice](https://mathoverflow.net/users/125498/leechlattice) shows that
$h(n) \ll n^{\frac 2 3}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.known_upper :
    (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3) := by
  sorry

open Real

/--
Estimate $h(n)$ by finding a better upper bound.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.better_upper :
    let upper_bound : ℕ → ℝ := answer(sorry)
    (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] upper_bound ∧
    upper_bound =o[atTop] fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3) := by
  sorry

/--
Estimate $h(n)$ by finding a better lower bound.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.better_lower:
    let lower_bound : ℕ → ℝ := answer(sorry)
    (lower_bound =O[atTop] fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ c > 0,
    (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12))) =O[atTop] (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) →
    ∀ c > 0, (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12))) =o[atTop] lower_bound := by
  sorry

/--
The observation of Zachary Hunter in [that question](https://mathoverflow.net/q/410808)
coupled with the bounds of Kelley-Meka [KeMe23](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.05537) imply that
$$h(N) \gg \exp(c(\log N)^{\frac 1 {12}})$$
for some $c > 0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.variants.known_lower :
    ∃ c > 0, (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12)))
    =O[atTop] fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ):= by
  sorry

end Erdos160

status_issues.recorded: @[category research open], with answer(sorry) for the improved lower-bound function.
status_issues.source_status: This particular improvement benchmark was already met by Bloom–Sisask’s September 2023 improvement of the three-term-progression density bound, combined with Hunter’s observation cited in the file. It does not settle the broader problem of estimating h optimally.
status_issues.evidence: Bloom–Sisask, arXiv:2309.02353, Theorem 1, states that a three-term-AP-free A⊆{1,…,N} satisfies |A|≤N exp(-d(log N)^(1/9)) for an absolute d>0. Hunter’s observation at https://mathoverflow.net/questions/410808 shows that each colour class restricted to the first floor(2N/3) integers must be three-term-AP-free. Hence h(N)≫exp(d'(log N)^(1/9)) for some d'>0. Taking L(N)=exp((log N)^(1/10)) gives L=O(h) and, for every c>0, exp(c(log N)^(1/12))=o(L), since 1/12<1/10<1/9. The exponent comparisons and implication from the improved h-bound to the exact Lean predicate were checked in /workspace/review/status_witness.lean.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change this declaration to category research solved, cite Bloom–Sisask, and replace its answer with `answer(fun n => Real.exp (Real.log (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10)))`. Keep the general estimation problem separate from this now-solved benchmark.

reformulations.difference: Lean follows MathOverflow’s minimum avoiding-colouring convention, whereas Erdős’s original paper defines the largest number of classes for which every partition has a four-term progression in the union of two classes. Lean also expresses avoidance by requiring at least three colours on every four-term progression.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a fixed colouring, a four-term progression lies in two colour fibres exactly when it uses at most two colours; this predicate equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/partition_equiv.lean. Passing between colourings and partitions, and removing unused colours when minimizing, preserves the minimum. The minimum avoiding threshold H is the original maximum unavoidable threshold G plus one. For n≥4, G≥2, so G≤H≤(3/2)G. Consequently G and H are of the same asymptotic order. Every occurrence of h in the file is in a Big-O relation, so this constant shift preserves all four theorem statements, including their conditions on possible answers. The full threshold-shift equivalence was checked mathematically, not formalized in Lean.

reformulations.difference: The improvement requirement is written conditionally, with an outer constant c witnessing an old lower bound and a newly bound inner c ranging over all positive constants.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write E_c(n)=exp(c(log n)^(1/12)). The separately stated known_lower supplies c₀>0 with E_c₀=O(h). Applying the conditional clause to c₀ yields ∀d>0, E_d=o(lower_bound). Conversely, this unconditional domination immediately implies the conditional clause. Thus the entire predicate is equivalent to lower_bound=O(h) ∧ ∀d>0, E_d=o(lower_bound), and the implication is not vacuous. This equivalence, under the known lower-bound hypothesis, was proved in /workspace/review/quantifiers.lean.

review.notes:
All five declarations were inspected, including the AP, cardinality, infimum, asymptotic, and answer definitions. Lean checks establish admissible colourings for every n, attainment of the minimum, h(0)=0, h(1)=h(2)=h(3)=1, and exclusion of palettes with fewer than three colours when n≥4. A computable finite-colouring check gives minima 0,1,1,1,3,3,3,3,3 for n=0,…,8. Further checks rule out zero or a fixed member of the old exponential family as answers to better_lower. Details and successful experiments are in /workspace/review/audit.md and the accompanying Lean files.

Source-access limitation: the live https://www.erdosproblems.com/160 and its forum returned Cloudflare HTTP 403 despite descriptive user agents. An archive index was accessible, but snapshot retrieval failed. The mathematical comparison therefore used the linked MathOverflow discussion and the original Erdős paper, together with the cited and subsequent literature. Any newer status annotation for better_upper on the live page remains unchecked. The target file was not modified.
